title: KV + Dynamic Batching + Kernel experiments — Week 9 notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick sync notes from the serving-runtime squad for Week 9 — focused on three concurrent threads: kernel micro-optimizations, KV cache eviction/lookup tweaks, and dynamic batching strategy iterations. This is a working log: experiments, surprising findings, and immediate action items.

Attendees:
- Jordan Patel (owner)
- Aisha Narang
- Diego Martínez
- Priya Rao
- Samir Gupta
- Guests: infra-oncall for kernel rollout testing

High-level summary:
- Kernel micro-optimizations are showing ~6-12% throughput uplift on medium-length contexts (512–1024) after A/B-ing the new fused-attn kernel, but introduced an AVX miscompilation on an older instance SKU that caused rare P50 regressions. We rolled the kernel to a canary pool and temporarily enabled the fallback path.
- KV cache: changed lookup path to a compacted hash table with open addressing (experiment branch). This reduced per-request CPU overhead by ~18% in the synthetic prefix-heavy workload but added a 1.4% memory overhead. Eviction heuristics (time-decay + usage count) are promising for LRU-like workloads.
- Dynamic batching: implemented a token-aware aggregator that weights requests by expected token cost (based on prompt length + predicted generation). In latency SLO simulations, the token-aware aggregator cuts average per-token latency by 9% without hurting throughput.

Detailed notes and results:
1) Kernel experiments (PR #1482)
- Change: fused-attn kernel that minimizes materialization of intermediate tensors and keeps KV layout contiguous across heads. Implemented opt path for fp16 packing (no quantization).
- Test harness: local perf rig + canary pool with 4xA100 and 8xV100 instances. Workloads: short-chat (64 tokens responses), medium-context generation (512 tokens), long-context retrieval (2–4k tokens).
- Results:
  * Medium-context throughput: +8–12% (median across runs).
  * Short-chat P99: no change (dominated by RPC + dispatch).
  * Long-context: small improvement for KV-heavy ops (~6%), but observed occasional P50 regressions on one older CPU SKU.
- Root cause for regression: code path used AVX512 instructions on machines that have a buggy microcode/older glibc shim; fallback to scalar path fixes it.
- Decision: gate fused-attn kernel behind a CPU-capability check in the runtime and keep canary pool until next week. Continue testing with upgraded microcode images.

2) KV cache changes
- Branch: kv-compact-hash (internal).
- Change: replace chained-hash buckets with linear probing style compact table; store small per-entry metadata to speed hits. Eviction: combine time-decay score (alpha) with use-count multiplier to adapt to bursty vs steady prefixes.
- Trade-offs observed: CPU per-request lower (~18%), mem usage +1.4% due to denser representation + probe tracking. Under heavy churn (many unique prefixes) eviction churn caused perf jitter — tuned probe length cap to reduce jitter.
- Metrics:
  * Hit latency: -14% median
  * Hit rate: unchanged for steady-state traces, +2% for prefix-repetition traces
  * Eviction churn: +9% before probe cap, stable after tuning
- Risks: compaction means slower cold-starts for new connections; plan to keep an opt-in flag for Dedicated customers for a release cycle.

3) Dynamic batching improvements
- Prototype: token-aware aggregator that estimates cost = prompt_tokens + expected_generated_tokens (historical average per model/route). Batches are formed subject to max_token_capacity and latency window.
- Simulation on production traces: token-aware wins over request-count-aware batcher for mixed-length traffic by reducing average queueing latency and improving model throughput per GPU.
- Key numbers:
  * Avg queuing latency: -11%
  * P95 end-to-end latency: -4% (stable)
  * Throughput (tokens/sec): +5% for mixed workloads
- Edge cases: occasional starvation of tiny requests when there is a backpressure of long continuations. Mitigation: weight tiny requests with a minimal priority credit that ensures periodic flushes.

Open incidents and debug notes:
- LINEAR-3921: regression during canary kernel rollout (see PR #1482). Incident timeline and root cause described. Current status: mitigated via fallback, patch queued.
- Observability gap: KV cache eviction churn spikes did not emit clear alerts. Action: add eviction-rate and probe-length histograms to per-route metrics (see action items).

Meeting decisions:
- Keep fused-attn kernel behind capability gate and extend canary for one more week while infra performs microcode updates on affected SKUs.
- Promote kv-compact-hash to internal staging for Dedicated testing; do not flip default for hosted customers yet.
- Merge token-aware aggregator behind a feature flag with AB testing on 10% of traffic for next two weeks.

Action items (owner — due):
- Jordan: coordinate with infra to schedule microcode/glibc image update on canary SKUs (due 2026-03-11).
- Aisha: open follow-up PR to add capability-gate checks and better CPU feature detection (due 2026-03-06) — PR drafted.
- Diego: add eviction-rate and probe-length histograms to telemetry and set an alert threshold (due 2026-03-10).
- Priya: run Dedicated workload tests for kv-compact-hash branch and collect memory/latency traces (due 2026-03-12).
- Samir: implement minimum-priority credit to avoid tiny-request starvation in token-aware aggregator (due 2026-03-09).

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Consider a small quantized fallback kernel for very long-context KV-heavy generations (experiment later this quarter).
- Revisit batching flush heuristics if we roll to more aggressive token caps — need to simulate under 99th percentile peak.
- Prepare a short explainer for product/solutions (2 slides) showing customer impact of these changes (cost per token improvement + latency SLO risk).

Appendix (quick links):
- Kernel PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1482
- Incident: LINEAR-3921
- Staging trace: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/kv-batching-experiments-wk9

End of week 9 notes. If anything important missing ping me in #eng-serving-runtime or drop comments on the PR.
